POST /api/v1/inbound/orders Tell us what inbound stock to expect (an ASN): PO number, expected delivery date, and SKUs with quantities, plus the lot number where your items are lot-tracked. One element per line. Each element of orders is one PO line: clientcode, ponumber, deliverydate, sku and quantity are required. Send JSON. A Content-Type other than application/json is answered 415. Validation accumulates: a 400 lists every problem it found for a line, not just the first. quantity must be a whole number above 0. deliverydate must be a real date (US Eastern). unitofmeasure, source, externalOrderId and rmaId are accepted for compatibility but not used. Existing integrations. POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel Cancel an order by its pick ticket ID. This works only before the order has shipping or tracking information and while it is still open; otherwise the response says the order could not be cancelled. Cancel by your pick ticket. The response is 200 whenever the request is valid; read order_cancelled to see whether it worked. Orders are created in the background, usually within seconds of a successful submit. Until then, cancel answers that the order cannot be cancelled: wait a few seconds and try again. Only open orders with no shipping or tracking information can be cancelled. Assembly orders cannot be cancelled through the API, and cancel finds only orders placed under your own owner code (not a related account's). If the order had already been released to the warehouse, a successful cancel marks it "do not ship" in Capacity, but contact Capacity Support straight away so the warehouse can stop it. Keep pick tickets unique. If two open orders share one, which order is cancelled is not defined. Existing integrations. Integrations built against the previous Capacity REST API may keep calling POST /api/order/cancel, at api-integration.capacityllc.com or api-partner.capacityllc.com, with the same request and response. New integrations must use this path; a new integration calling the previous path gets 410.
Responses​ 200 400 401 500 OK Bad Request Unauthorized Internal Server Error

POST /api/v1/outbound/orders Send one or more outbound orders for fulfilment. Each valid order in the request is accepted even if others fail; a 400 response names one order that failed and why (not every failure), so fix the orders that failed and resend only those. Values are strings and names are lowercase. Quantities, amounts and flags are all strings ("2", not 2). Quantities are whole numbers, digits only. Required per order: the fields marked required, plus shipname or shipbusinessname (at least one), and at least one line. An order with an empty lines array is skipped. Always send lines: an order sent without the field is accepted with no lines. Defaults: an empty or omitted retailercode becomes WEB, and empty or omitted single-character flags become N. A flag that is only spaces is rejected. itemproductid, buyeritemnumber and itemproductdesc longer than 50 characters are cut to 50 rather than rejected. Partial acceptance: when individual orders fail validation, every valid order in the request is still accepted, and the 400 names one failed order and its reason (not every failure). Fix and resend only the orders that failed. Nothing is accepted when the 400 is Invalid Input, Unable to validate client., or Please validate order data. with no detail (a null order or line, or no order with lines). 500 or 504 with {"accepted": false}: some orders may not have been accepted. Resending the same request within 24 hours is generally safe: orders already accepted with identical content are recognised and skipped. Some accounts receive 504 instead of 500; treat them the same. Do not retry automatically after a timeout with no response. The orders may have been accepted in full, and this API does not return order IDs you could check. Contact Capacity Support with the time of the request, the pick tickets and the X-Correlation-ID you sent. Dates (orderdate, requestedshipdate, canceldate, requesteddeliverydate, deliverybydate) are read as US Eastern dates. Use YYYY-MM-DD. A requestedshipdate more than 3 days out normally holds the order as a future order until nearer the date. Existing integrations. Integrations built against the previous Capacity REST API may keep calling POST /api/order/create, at api-integration.capacityllc.com or api-partner.capacityllc.com, with the same request and response. New integrations must use this path; a new integration calling the previous path gets 410.
Responses​ 200 400 401 500 504 OK Bad Request Unauthorized Internal Server Error Gateway Timeout

POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/status Your picked orders (status: picked, awaiting shipment) with their lines, cartons and tracking. Every order of yours that is currently picked is returned, plus the Capacity order IDs you send if they have been picked; orders belonging to related accounts (same parent client) are included. A requested ID that has not been picked, or does not exist, comes back as a "not found" entry; if nothing is found the response is 404. This returns picked orders. An order appears once it has been picked (and until it ships). Every order of yours that is currently picked is returned, even ones you did not ask for, plus the orders you ask for by Capacity order number (orderIds) if they have been picked. Orders belonging to your related accounts (same parent client) are included. An order that exists but has not been picked yet comes back as a "not found" entry. If nothing at all is found, the response is 404. Use shipment confirmations, not this call, to learn what has shipped. orderIds are Capacity order numbers (as returned in capacityOrderNum by carrier tracking events), not your pick tickets. orderStatusDate and pickedOrderStatusDate are YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmm; releaseDate and currentSLADate are MM/DD/YYYY; all US Eastern with no offset. Existing integrations. Integrations built against the previous Capacity REST API may keep calling POST /api/order/status/picked, at api-integration.capacityllc.com or api-partner.capacityllc.com, with the same request and response. New integrations must use this path; a new integration calling the previous path gets 410.
Responses​ 200 400 401 404 500 OK Bad Request Unauthorized Not Found Internal Server Error

POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/shipments Ship confirmations for your orders for the batch number and batch date you send (both required): what shipped, order totals, carrier, service and tracking numbers. Polling, not callbacks. Capacity prepares ship confirmations in numbered batches each day (batch_num 1, 2, 3 ...). Your onboarding contact tells you how many batches your account receives per day. Request each batch for a batch_date after it has been prepared, and match lines to your orders by pickticketid. Batch 1 starts the evening before. Batches are keyed on when the confirmation was created (US Eastern), not the ship time. Batch 1 of a date covers confirmations created from 22:00 the previous evening; the other batches cover the calendar date. A confirmation created at 22:30 on 2 November is in batch 1 of 3 November. One item per order line. shipDate is ISO 8601 without an offset (US Eastern). expiryDate is MM/DD/YYYY, or empty when there is none. No data is a 200. When a batch has no confirmations, the response is 200 {"message": "No records found. Please check input."}, not an empty list. Check the body before reading it as data. Existing integrations. Integrations built against the previous Capacity REST API may keep calling POST /api/order/track, at api-integration.capacityllc.com or api-partner.capacityllc.com, with the same request and response. New integrations must use this path; a new integration calling the previous path gets 410.

Poll by hour. hour_num is the hour of day, 0-23, in US Eastern time (0 is midnight to 00:59). batch_date is the Eastern calendar date. POST /api/v1/auth/token Exchange your client ID and secret for a bearer token. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <token> on every other call. Tokens last about 15 minutes; expires_in in the response gives the exact number of seconds. Form post, not JSON. Send grant_type=client_credentials with your client_id and client_secret, either as form fields or as an HTTP Basic Authorization header (client_id:client_secret, base64). If both are present, the header is used. Secrets are case-sensitive. Reuse the token. It lasts about 15 minutes (expires_in, in seconds). Cache it and request a new one shortly before it expires; do not request a token per call. Errors use the OAuth shape, not {"message": ...}: 400 {"error": "invalid_credentials", "error_description": ...}, 400 {"error": "unsupported_grant_type"}, and 503 {"error": "temporarily_unavailable", "error_description": ...} when the token service is briefly unavailable (retry with backoff). Existing integrations. Integrations built against the previous Capacity REST API may keep calling POST /Token, at api-integration.capacityllc.com or api-partner.capacityllc.com, with the same request and response. New integrations must use this path; a new integration calling the previous path gets 410.
Responses​ 200 400 503 OK Bad Request Service Unavailable

The Partner API uses the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow. Your integration exchanges a client ID and secret for a short-lived access token, then sends that token on every request. Your system Capacity Partner API | POST /api/v1/auth/token | | client_id + client_secret ------------------> | | <------------------ access_token (~15 min) | | | | GET /api/v1/ping | | Authorization: Bearer <access_token> -------> | | <------------------------------ 200 / 401 |

Credential Format Notes Client ID Text, issued by Capacity Not secret, but do not publish it. Client secret Text, issued by Capacity Secret and case-sensitive. Sandbox and production credentials are issued separately. See Environments.

POST /api/v1/auth/token with a form body (application/x-www-form-urlencoded): Field Value grant_type client_credentials (the only grant supported) client_id Your client ID client_secret Your client secret You can send the ID and secret as an HTTP Basic Authorization header instead of form fields. If you send both, the header is used. cURL # Form fields curl -X POST "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token" \ -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \ --data-urlencode "grant_type=client_credentials" \ --data-urlencode "client_id=$CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID" \ --data-urlencode "client_secret=$CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET" # Or HTTP Basic curl -X POST "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token" \ -u "$CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID:$CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET" \ -d "grant_type=client_credentials" The response: Field Meaning access_token The token. Treat it as an opaque string: do not parse it or rely on its contents. token_type Always bearer. expires_in Seconds until the token expires (about 900). .issued, .expires When the token was issued and expires, as RFC 1123 dates in GMT.
Send it on every request except the token request: Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9.EXAMPLE-ONLY.signature

Request a token once and reuse it until about 60 seconds before it expires. Requesting a token for every call is slower for you and may be limited in future. Node.js Python C# let cached = { token: null, expiresAt: 0 }; async function getToken() { if (cached.token && Date.now() < cached.expiresAt - 60_000) { return cached.token; } const response = await fetch("https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token", { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }, body: new URLSearchParams({ grant_type: "client_credentials", client_id: process.env.CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID, client_secret: process.env.CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET, }), }); if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Token request failed: ${response.status}`); const body = await response.json(); cached = { token: body.access_token, expiresAt: Date.now() + body.expires_in * 1000 }; return cached.token; } import os, time, requests _cached = {"token": None, "expires_at": 0.0} def get_token() -> str: if _cached["token"] and time.time() < _cached["expires_at"] - 60: return _cached["token"] response = requests.post( "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token", data={ "grant_type": "client_credentials", "client_id": os.environ["CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID"], "client_secret": os.environ["CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET"], }, timeout=30, ) response.raise_for_status() body = response.json() _cached.update(token=body["access_token"], expires_at=time.time() + body["expires_in"]) return _cached["token"] public sealed class CapacityTokenProvider(HttpClient http, string clientId, string clientSecret) { private readonly SemaphoreSlim gate = new(1, 1); private string? token; private DateTimeOffset expiresAt; public async Task<string> GetTokenAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { await gate.WaitAsync(cancellationToken); try { if (token is not null && DateTimeOffset.UtcNow < expiresAt.AddSeconds(-60)) { return token; } using var response = await http.PostAsync("https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token", new FormUrlEncodedContent(new Dictionary<string, string> { ["grant_type"] = "client_credentials", ["client_id"] = clientId, ["client_secret"] = clientSecret, }), cancellationToken); response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode(); using var json = JsonDocument.Parse(await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(cancellationToken)); token = json.RootElement.GetProperty("access_token").GetString()!; expiresAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddSeconds(json.RootElement.GetProperty("expires_in").GetInt32()); return token; } finally { gate.Release(); } } } If a call returns 401, the token may have expired early or been revoked. Get a new token and retry the call once. If it fails again, stop and check your credentials.

Response Cause Fix 400 {"error": "invalid_credentials", ...} Wrong or missing client ID or secret, or the credentials are disabled. Check both values and the case of the secret. Check you are not using sandbox credentials in production. 400 {"error": "unsupported_grant_type"} grant_type is missing or not client_credentials. Send grant_type=client_credentials. 503 {"error": "temporarily_unavailable", ...} The token service is briefly unavailable. Retry after a few seconds, with backoff. 401 on any other call Missing, malformed or expired token. Get a new token and retry once.

Store the secret in a secrets manager or an environment variable. Never commit it or write it to logs. Call the API from your servers only. Never put the secret in a browser, mobile app or anything a customer can download. Do not share one credential between unrelated systems; ask for a separate one. If a secret may have been exposed, contact Capacity Support straight away so it can be replaced.

Integrations built for the previous Capacity REST API, at api-integration.capacityllc.com, may keep calling POST /Token with their existing credentials. It behaves the same as POST /api/v1/auth/token. New integrations must use POST /api/v1/auth/token at api-partner.capacityllc.com. See Existing integrations.

The Partner API has two environments. They have different base URLs, different credentials and different data. Nothing you do in one affects the other. Sandbox Production Base URL https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com https://api-partner.capacityllc.com Credentials Sandbox client ID and secret Production client ID and secret Data Test data. Orders are not fulfilled or shipped to real customers. Live. Orders are picked, packed and shipped. Use it for Building and testing your integration Your live integration, after go-live Use the Sandbox | Production switch at the top of every page to change the base URL in all code samples. The coloured band under the navigation bar shows which one is selected. New integrations must use api-partner.capacityllc.com. Capacity does not support new integrations at any other address.

Integrations built against the previous Capacity REST API call https://api-integration.capacityllc.com. That address is moving to this same API, so existing integrations keep working without changes: The previous paths (for example POST /api/order/create and POST /Token) keep working for existing integrations at both api-integration.capacityllc.com and api-partner.capacityllc.com. The request and response formats do not change. api-integration.capacityllc.com is for existing integrations only. It is not offered to new clients. Capacity will ask existing integrations to move to api-partner.capacityllc.com and the /api/v1/ paths. See Paths and versions and the legacy path map in the API reference.

Keep the base URL in configuration. Your code should read one setting for the base URL and one for each credential. Going live, or moving from api-integration to api-partner, is then a configuration change, not a code change. Never mix the pairs. A sandbox token is rejected by production and a production token is rejected by the sandbox. A configuration that points production credentials at the sandbox URL fails in a way that is easy to misread as "wrong password". Label your logs. Log which environment each request went to, and the X-Correlation-ID you sent.

Every current path starts with /api/v1/. Paths without /v1/ (for example /api/order/create) belong to the previous Capacity REST API and are kept only for integrations built against it. A new integration that calls one gets 410 Gone with the current path in the message. See the API reference, where those paths are marked deprecated.

Email itedi@capacityllc.com to request Partner API sandbox credentials. You receive: Item Example in these docs What it is Client ID YOUR_SANDBOX_CLIENT_ID Identifies your integration. Client secret YOUR_SANDBOX_CLIENT_SECRET A password for your integration. Case-sensitive. Owner code ZZ The 2-character code for your account. You send it as clientcode on orders and client on inventory requests. Ship method and retailer codes GROUND, WEB The codes agreed for your account during onboarding. Sandbox and production credentials are different. Sandbox credentials do not work in production, and production credentials do not work in the sandbox. Keep the secret out of code Load the client secret from an environment variable or a secrets manager. Never commit it, put it in a URL, or send it from a browser. The samples read the credentials from environment variables: export CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID="YOUR_SANDBOX_CLIENT_ID" export CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET="YOUR_SANDBOX_CLIENT_SECRET"

Exchange the client ID and secret for a bearer token. The request is a form post, not JSON. cURL Node.js Python C# curl -X POST "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token" \ -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \ --data-urlencode "grant_type=client_credentials" \ --data-urlencode "client_id=$CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID" \ --data-urlencode "client_secret=$CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET" \ -H "X-Correlation-ID: $(uuidgen)" const response = await fetch("https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token", { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", "X-Correlation-ID": crypto.randomUUID(), }, body: new URLSearchParams({ grant_type: "client_credentials", client_id: process.env.CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID, client_secret: process.env.CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET, }), }); console.log(response.status, await response.json()); import os import uuid import requests response = requests.post( "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token", headers={ "X-Correlation-ID": str(uuid.uuid4()), }, data={ "grant_type": "client_credentials", "client_id": os.environ["CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID"], "client_secret": os.environ["CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET"], }, timeout=60, ) print(response.status_code, response.json()) using var http = new HttpClient(); using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token"); request.Headers.Add("X-Correlation-ID", Guid.NewGuid().ToString()); request.Content = new FormUrlEncodedContent(new Dictionary<string, string> { ["grant_type"] = "client_credentials", ["client_id"] = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID")!, ["client_secret"] = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET")!, }); using var response = await http.SendAsync(request); Console.WriteLine($"{(int)response.StatusCode} {await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync()}"); Expected response · 200 { "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9.EXAMPLE-ONLY.signature", "token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": 899, ".issued": "Mon, 02 Nov 2026 14:00:00 GMT", ".expires": "Mon, 02 Nov 2026 14:14:59 GMT" } Keep the access_token for the next steps: export CAPACITY_TOKEN="paste the access_token here" The token lasts about 15 minutes. Reuse it until shortly before expires_in runs out; do not request a new token for every call. See Authentication for token caching. If you get It means Do this 400 invalid_credentials The client ID or secret is wrong, or the credentials are disabled. Check both values, including the case of the secret. Check you are using sandbox credentials against the sandbox. 400 unsupported_grant_type grant_type is not client_credentials. Send grant_type=client_credentials. 503 temporarily_unavailable The token service is briefly unavailable. Wait a few seconds and retry.

cURL Node.js Python C# curl "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/ping" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $CAPACITY_TOKEN" \ -H "X-Correlation-ID: $(uuidgen)" const response = await fetch("https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/ping", { method: "GET", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.CAPACITY_TOKEN}`, "X-Correlation-ID": crypto.randomUUID(), }, }); console.log(response.status, await response.json()); import os import uuid import requests response = requests.get( "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/ping", headers={ "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CAPACITY_TOKEN']}", "X-Correlation-ID": str(uuid.uuid4()), }, timeout=60, ) print(response.status_code, response.json()) using var http = new HttpClient(); using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/ping"); request.Headers.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("CAPACITY_TOKEN")!); request.Headers.Add("X-Correlation-ID", Guid.NewGuid().ToString()); using var response = await http.SendAsync(request); Console.WriteLine($"{(int)response.StatusCode} {await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync()}"); Expected response · 200 "Connection is successful." A 401 with {"message": "Authorization has been denied for this request."} means the header is missing, malformed (it must be Bearer, a space, then the token) or the token has expired. Get a new token and try again.

Send one order with one line. Replace the owner, retailer and ship method codes with yours, and use a SKU that exists for your account. The ship date is a week out, so the order waits as a future order and you can cancel it in the next step. cURL Node.js Python C# curl -X POST "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/outbound/orders" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $CAPACITY_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-Correlation-ID: $(uuidgen)" \ -d '{ "orders": [ { "pickticketid": "PT-0001001", "clientcode": "ZZ", "retailercode": "WEB", "shipname": "Jordan Example", "shipaddress1": "100 Example Street", "shipcity": "Edison", "shipstate": "NJ", "shipzip": "08817", "shipcountry": "US", "shipresidentialflag": "Y", "shipmethod": "GROUND", "requestedshipdate": "2026-11-09", "lines": [ { "itemlinenumber": "1", "itemproductid": "SKU-EXAMPLE-1", "itemorderquantity": "1" } ] } ] }' const response = await fetch("https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/outbound/orders", { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.CAPACITY_TOKEN}`, "Content-Type": "application/json", "X-Correlation-ID": crypto.randomUUID(), }, body: JSON.stringify({ "orders": [ { "pickticketid": "PT-0001001", "clientcode": "ZZ", "retailercode": "WEB", "shipname": "Jordan Example", "shipaddress1": "100 Example Street", "shipcity": "Edison", "shipstate": "NJ", "shipzip": "08817", "shipcountry": "US", "shipresidentialflag": "Y", "shipmethod": "GROUND", "requestedshipdate": "2026-11-09", "lines": [ { "itemlinenumber": "1", "itemproductid": "SKU-EXAMPLE-1", "itemorderquantity": "1" } ] } ] }), }); console.log(response.status, await response.json()); import os import uuid import requests response = requests.post( "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/outbound/orders", headers={ "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CAPACITY_TOKEN']}", "X-Correlation-ID": str(uuid.uuid4()), }, json={ "orders": [ { "pickticketid": "PT-0001001", "clientcode": "ZZ", "retailercode": "WEB", "shipname": "Jordan Example", "shipaddress1": "100 Example Street", "shipcity": "Edison", "shipstate": "NJ", "shipzip": "08817", "shipcountry": "US", "shipresidentialflag": "Y", "shipmethod": "GROUND", "requestedshipdate": "2026-11-09", "lines": [ { "itemlinenumber": "1", "itemproductid": "SKU-EXAMPLE-1", "itemorderquantity": "1", }, ], }, ], }, timeout=60, ) print(response.status_code, response.json()) using var http = new HttpClient(); using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/outbound/orders"); request.Headers.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("CAPACITY_TOKEN")!); request.Headers.Add("X-Correlation-ID", Guid.NewGuid().ToString()); request.Content = new StringContent(""" { "orders": [ { "pickticketid": "PT-0001001", "clientcode": "ZZ", "retailercode": "WEB", "shipname": "Jordan Example", "shipaddress1": "100 Example Street", "shipcity": "Edison", "shipstate": "NJ", "shipzip": "08817", "shipcountry": "US", "shipresidentialflag": "Y", "shipmethod": "GROUND", "requestedshipdate": "2026-11-09", "lines": [ { "itemlinenumber": "1", "itemproductid": "SKU-EXAMPLE-1", "itemorderquantity": "1" } ] } ] } """, Encoding.UTF8, "application/json"); using var response = await http.SendAsync(request); Console.WriteLine($"{(int)response.StatusCode} {await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync()}"); Expected response · 200 { "accepted": true } Every value in an order is a string, including quantities ("1", not 1). Field names are lowercase. If an order fails validation you get a 400 that names the field and the pick ticket: { "message": "Please validate order data. Shipping Address 1 can not be empty for Pick Ticket Id PT-0001001" } Other valid orders in the same request are still accepted. Fix the order the message names and resend only that order. (When the message is Invalid Input or names no order, nothing was accepted.) The full field list and every response are in Submit orders.

Orders are created in the background, usually within seconds. If cancel answers that the order cannot be cancelled, wait a few seconds and try again. cURL Node.js Python C# curl -X POST "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $CAPACITY_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-Correlation-ID: $(uuidgen)" \ -d '{ "pickticketid": "PT-0001001" }' const response = await fetch("https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel", { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.CAPACITY_TOKEN}`, "Content-Type": "application/json", "X-Correlation-ID": crypto.randomUUID(), }, body: JSON.stringify({ "pickticketid": "PT-0001001" }), }); console.log(response.status, await response.json()); import os import uuid import requests response = requests.post( "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel", headers={ "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CAPACITY_TOKEN']}", "X-Correlation-ID": str(uuid.uuid4()), }, json={ "pickticketid": "PT-0001001", }, timeout=60, ) print(response.status_code, response.json()) using var http = new HttpClient(); using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel"); request.Headers.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("CAPACITY_TOKEN")!); request.Headers.Add("X-Correlation-ID", Guid.NewGuid().ToString()); request.Content = new StringContent(""" { "pickticketid": "PT-0001001" } """, Encoding.UTF8, "application/json"); using var response = await http.SendAsync(request); Console.WriteLine($"{(int)response.StatusCode} {await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync()}"); Expected response · 200 { "pickticketid": "PT-0001001", "order_cancelled": true, "order_cancelled_result": "Order cancelled successfully." } What "cancelled" means Cancel only works while the order is open and has no shipping or tracking information. Pick tickets should be unique: if two open orders share one, which order is cancelled is not defined.

Before you switch to production: Request production credentials. They are separate from your sandbox credentials. Change the base URL to the production URL. Keep it in configuration, not in code. Store the secret in a secrets manager, not in source control or logs. Reuse one token until shortly before it expires. Treat every date and time from the API as US Eastern time. See Dates and time zones. Retry 500, 503 and 504 with backoff, and send an X-Correlation-ID on every request so support can find it. See Errors.

Dates and times are US Eastern, with no offset Capacity operates on US Eastern time (America/New_York, EST/EDT). Every order, shipment, inventory and receiving date the Partner API accepts or returns is Eastern wall-clock time, and no time-zone offset is included. Convert explicitly; do not assume UTC. The one exception is the token's .issued and .expires, which are GMT.

Batch dates (batch_date) are Eastern calendar dates. Ship-confirmation batches are keyed on when the confirmation was created, and batch 1 of a date starts at 22:00 the previous evening: a confirmation created at 22:30 on 2 November is in batch 1 of 3 November. Other batches cover the calendar date. Hours (hour_num on tracking events) are Eastern hours, 0–23. 0 is midnight to 00:59 Eastern. Dates you send on orders (orderdate, requestedshipdate, and so on) are read as Eastern dates. Daylight saving time applies. Eastern is UTC−5 in winter and UTC−4 in summer.

The API keeps the formats of the previous Capacity REST API, so they differ by field: Where Example Format Shipment shipDate; lot expiryDate (inventory by lot and LPN) 2026-11-02T00:00:00 ISO 8601, no offset. A lot with no expiry shows 0001-01-01T00:00:00. Shipment and carton expiryDate; picked-order releaseDate, currentSLADate 11/02/2026 MM/DD/YYYY; empty when not set Picked-order orderStatusDate, pickedOrderStatusDate 2026-11-02 14:05:09.123 YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmm Receipt expirydate 2026-11-02 YYYY-MM-DD Receipt receivedate 2026-11-02 YYYY-MM-DD; the time of your request, not of the receipt Token .issued, .expires Mon, 02 Nov 2026 14:00:00 GMT RFC 1123, GMT When you send dates, use YYYY-MM-DD or ISO 8601 (2026-11-02T15:30:00) without an offset.

Most errors from data endpoints are a JSON object with a message: { "message": "Please validate order data. Shipping Address 1 can not be empty for Pick Ticket Id PT-0001001" } Two exceptions: the token endpoint uses the OAuth error shape, and a failed order save on Submit orders returns {"accepted": false} (see Retrying order submissions). { "error": "invalid_credentials", "error_description": "A valid client_Id and client_Secret must be provided." } Read the HTTP status first, then the message. Messages are written for people; match on the status code in your code, not on message text.

Status Meaning Retry? What to do 200 Success. — Some read endpoints also return 200 when nothing matched; see No data is not an error. 400 The request is invalid: malformed JSON, a missing or invalid field, or your account could not be validated. No Fix the request. Validation messages name the field and the pick ticket. 401 Missing, malformed or expired token. Once, with a new token Get a new token and retry once. If it fails again, check your credentials. 404 None of the orders you asked for has been picked, and none is currently picked (Get picked orders). No Check the IDs; use shipment confirmations for shipped orders. 410 You called a path kept only for older integrations. No Use the current /api/v1/ path named in the message. 415 The Content-Type is not JSON. Returned only by Submit orders, Submit receiving orders, Get receipt confirmations, Get inventory and Get inventory by lot and LPN. No Send Content-Type: application/json (text/json is also accepted). 500 Something failed on our side. Yes, with backoff Retry. For order submission, see Retrying order submissions. 503 A service we depend on is briefly unavailable. Yes, with backoff Retry after a few seconds. 504 Returned instead of 500 for some accounts when orders could not be saved. Yes, with backoff Treat exactly like 500. The Partner API does not currently return 403, 409 or 429. Handle any other 4xx as "do not retry" and any other 5xx as "retry with backoff", so your integration keeps working if new codes are introduced.

When nothing matches, some read endpoints answer 200 with a message instead of an empty list: { "message": "No records found. Please check input." } Check the shape of a 200 body before you read it as data.
documents.s: No data is not an error

documents.t: Order submission is the one call where a retry could create duplicates, so it is handled specially: After a 400 that names an order, the orders that passed validation were accepted. Fix the order named in the message and resend only the orders that failed. After Invalid Input, Unable to validate client., or Please validate order data. with no detail, nothing was accepted. After a 500 or 504 with {"accepted": false}, some orders may have been accepted. Resending the same request within 24 hours is generally safe: orders already accepted with identical content are recognised and skipped. After a timeout with no response at all, do not resend automatically: the orders may have been accepted in full, and the duplicate check above does not cover a request that succeeded. Contact Capacity Support with the time of the request, the pick tickets and the X-Correlation-ID you sent.
Wait 2 seconds before the first retry, then double the wait each time (2, 4, 8, 16 seconds), adding up to a second of random jitter. Stop after five attempts and alert someone.

Send an X-Correlation-ID header with a unique value (a UUID) on every request. It is returned on the response. Log it with the request, and when you contact support quote it together with the time of the request and, for orders, the pick tickets.

Integrations built against the previous Capacity REST API keep working. They can call these paths with the same requests and responses at api-integration.capacityllc.com or api-partner.capacityllc.com. New integrations must use the /api/v1/ paths; a new integration that calls a previous path gets 410 Gone with the current path in the message. Previous path (existing integrations) Use instead POST /Token POST /api/v1/auth/token GET /api/order GET /api/v1/ping GET /api/RO/connect GET /api/v1/ping POST /api/order/create POST /api/v1/outbound/orders POST /api/order/cancel POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel POST /api/order/status/picked POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/status POST /api/order/track POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/shipments POST /api/order/track/cartons POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/shipments/cartons POST /api/track/trackevent POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/shipments/tracking/events POST /api/RO/create POST /api/v1/inbound/orders POST /api/RO/track POST /api/v1/inbound/orders/confirmations POST /api/inventory POST /api/v1/inventory POST /api/inventory/storage/locations/qty POST /api/v1/inventory/lots-and-lpns POST /api/order/track/old No direct equivalent. Previous ship-confirmation format. No /api/v1/ equivalent: use POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/shipments, whose response format differs. POST /api/order/track/cartons/old No direct equivalent. Previous carton format. No /api/v1/ equivalent: use POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/shipments/cartons, whose response format differs.

Change the base URL to https://api-partner.capacityllc.com and the token path to /api/v1/auth/token. Your credentials do not change. Change each path using the table above. Request and response bodies are the same, except for the two paths with no direct equivalent. Keep sending the key body field (and apiversion, if you send it today) until Capacity confirms your credentials are set up as a current integration; current integrations send neither. Test in the sandbox before switching production.

Email the Capacity integrations team at itedi@capacityllc.com for: sandbox or production credentials replacing a credential that may have been exposed help with a failing request questions about the API if you are evaluating Capacity Existing clients with a production problem: email itsupport@capacityllc.com to open a support ticket, or contact your Capacity account manager.

Help us find your request quickly: The environment (sandbox or production) The method and path, for example POST /api/v1/outbound/orders The X-Correlation-ID you sent, and the time of the request (with time zone) The HTTP status and the response body Never include your client secret or an access token in a ticket or email.
